findings.evidence: Lines 42-45 `@[simp] theorem represents_iff ... Iff.rfl` and 55-58 `@[simp] theorem mem_unitValueSet ... ↔ Represents Q (a : R)`; the PR's own proof at line 124 uses `simpa only [mem_unitValueSet, ...]` rather than default simp, showing the default set is not usable here.
findings.fix: Drop `@[simp]` from `represents_iff` (keep it as the plain definitional restatement, usable via `rw`/`simp [represents_iff]`), leaving `Represents` as the simp normal form that `mem_unitValueSet` reduces to.
findings.issue: `@[simp] represents_iff` rewrites `Represents Q a` to `∃ v, Q v = a`, while `@[simp] mem_unitValueSet` (line 55) rewrites membership *to* `Represents`. Chained, `a ∈ unitValueSet Q` normalizes to `∃ v, Q v = ↑a`, so `represents_zero`, `mem_unitValueSet_mul_square_iff` and both criterion lemmas — all stated in terms of `Represents`/`∈ unitValueSet` — no longer match a simp-normalized goal.

findings.evidence: grep of the file shows no occurrence of `Equivalent` or `IsometryEquiv`; the roadmap target that consumes this API is stated modulo isometry: `roadmap/TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInvariants/README.md:646` `c ∈ unitValueSet ⟨a,b⟩ ↔ ⟨a,b⟩ ≅ ⟨c, abc⟩`, and README:113-120 makes `unitValueSet` the carrier of the classification statements.
findings.fix: Add `QuadraticMap.Equivalent.unitValueSet_eq` (and the `Represents` form, `e : IsometryEquiv Q Q' → (Represents Q a ↔ Represents Q' a)`), plus `Represents Q a → Represents (Q.prod Q') a`.
findings.issue: `Represents`/`unitValueSet` are introduced with no interaction with the operations in scope: no invariance under `QuadraticMap.Equivalent`/`IsometryEquiv`, and no monotonicity along `QuadraticMap.prod` (which the main criterion's statement itself uses). Without the first, `unitValueSet` is not usable as an invariant at all.

findings.evidence: Line 39 `theorem _root_.QuadraticMap.represents_zero (Q : QuadraticMap R M N) : Represents Q 0` has no attribute; the roadmap records this as the edge case every consumer meets (`README.md:626-631`, `697`).
findings.fix: Mark `represents_zero` `@[simp]` (it rewrites the closed proposition to `True` and cannot loop).
findings.issue: `represents_zero` is unconditionally true for every quadratic map but carries no automation annotation, so goals of the form `Represents Q 0` are not discharged automatically.

summary: The two `@[simp]` annotations define conflicting normal forms and unfold the new abstraction away, making the file's own `unitValueSet` lemmas unreachable by simp; the definitions also ship without the isometry-invariance lemma that makes `unitValueSet` an invariant.
